Conagra halved its dividend after a 38% five-year slide, and AT&T and Pfizer now show similar strain: AT&T's EPS trails its payout, Pfizer's free cash flow falls short.

Hormel's $1.17 dividend exceeds its fiscal 2026 GAAP EPS guidance of roughly $1 to $1 even as management touts a 392-quarter payout streak.

Before trusting a high yield after a price drop, check whether free cash flow covers the dividend without new borrowing.

The biggest 401k decisions tend to get made once and never revisited: when to roll it over, what to hold inside it, and when to start taking money out. That is exactly what the report: 401k & IRA Tips and Answers was created to address, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

A falling share price is information. When a stock slips for years while the board keeps declaring the same dividend and executives keep promising to protect it, the market and management are telling two different stories. Conagra Brands (NYSE:CAG) shows how that can end. Its quarterly payout dropped from $0.35 to $0.175, and the stock is down 38.24% over five years. If you buy a yield like that, you are taking the other side of the market's view, so it pays to know what each side is looking at.

gopixa / Getty Images

Here's the rule: a dividend is sustainable when earnings and free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending) cover it without new borrowing. When they don't, the payout is coming from debt.

Conagra Brands (CAG): A Case Where the Market Was Right

Conagra's forward yield is about 4.6% even after the cut. Management told analysts that rating agencies "looked at our cut of the dividend as a positive in terms of our credit rating and our position." The pressure did not end with the cut. First-quarter fiscal 2027 free cash flow came in at -$127.9 million, and leverage stood at 3.99 times against a three-times target. At today's prices, AT&T yields 5.0% and Eastman Chemical yields 5.2%.

AT&T plans to hold its dividend at $1.11 a share. Eastman's dividend grew 4.5% a year from fiscal 2020 to fiscal 2025.

AT&T's dividend is well covered, using 44% of its free cash flow over the 12 months to Sept. 30, 2026, against a tight 81% at Eastman.

Eastman cut its 2026 operating cash flow outlook to $850 million, while AT&T guides to free cash flow of $18 billion+ in 2026, rising to $21 billion+ in 2028.

AT&T (T:NYSE) told investors on Oct. 21 that it plans to keep its dividend at $1.11 a share a year. It also guided free cash flow higher every year through 2028, and that extra cash is going to $24 billion+ of share buybacks.

A week later, Eastman Chemical (EMN:NYSE) cut its 2026 operating cash flow outlook to $850 million from $900 million, citing the Middle East conflict's pressure on working capital. Its dividend has still grown 4.5% a year from fiscal 2020 to fiscal 2025.

At today's prices, the two yield 5.0% and 5.2%. So which would I rather hold for the next 20 years?

title: What Gave AT&T Stock Its Edge Over Verizon?

What Gave AT&T Stock Its Edge Over Verizon?

Today's big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash

Two companies in the same telecom industry grew their sales at about the same pace over the last three years. Over five years, however, one stock gained 58.2% and the other 22.5%. The bigger gain went to AT&T (T), and the smaller to Verizon Communications (VZ). Take a guess before reading on: did AT&T sell more, earn more per share, or get a higher price from investors for each dollar of profit?

Who Has Beaten Verizon Over Five Years?

Over the five years to November 2026, Verizon stock did better than 65.0% of the 20 companies in its industry. Yet AT&T, whose sales grew like Verizon's, finished 35.6 points ahead. Here is how the two compare on sales growth, earnings multiple and stock returns.

AT&T built that lead before the last year. Over the past twelve months, Verizon stock actually performed better than AT&T's.

Did AT&T Grow Faster Than Verizon?

No. AT&T and Verizon expanded at about the same pace over the last three years. AT&T's sales grew 1.9% a year on average, while Verizon's grew 1.3%. Over the full five years, Verizon's sales actually rose more, climbing 3.8% between 2021 and 2026, against 0.7% for AT&T.

The two also sell much the same thing. AT&T offers wireless voice and data communications services and broadband fiber to homes. Verizon reports mobility and broadband service revenue. Its Consumer segment brought in 77.3% of its revenue in fiscal 2025. Faster sales did not give AT&T its lead.

Where Did The Gap Come From?

The gap came from profit per share. Between the year to September 2021 and the year to September 2026, AT&T's earnings per share rose 2212.5%, while Verizon's fell 26.5%. Verizon also kept less of each sales dollar, with its operating margin down 3.0 points.

AT&T's operating margin rose only 1.1 points, so most of its gain came below operating profit. Its net income rose 1037.2% from a small 2021 profit. Its share count fell 8.8%. Together, those two account for only part of the rise in earnings per share.

Investors did not pay more for that profit. AT&T stock's earnings multiple fell between 2021 and today. Verizon's multiple went the other way, from 10.2 times in 2021 to 11.7 times today. So profit per share, not the multiple, made the difference.

Verizon is working on its costs. Management said on the fiscal Q3 2026 call that its cost reduction plan across operating and capital spending remains fully on track. It also said that promotional spending to win new customers fell 41% from a year earlier.

Fourth-Quarter Results In January

AT&T is expected to report its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results in January 2027. Management has said the release will outline the drivers behind its 2027 cash outlook. The quarter itself matters too, as management expects free cash flow of about $6 billion, compared with $4.2 billion a year earlier.

Fiber pricing is the weak spot. During the third quarter, fiber ARPU, the average revenue per fiber customer, fell 4% from a year earlier. Management tied the decline partly to its introductory pricing and expects a similar fall in the fourth quarter. Free cash flow and fiber revenue per customer are the two measures to watch in January.

AT&T's Debt Coming Due

At September 30, 2026, AT&T had $9.48 billion of long-term debt maturing within one year. That debt comes due while the company carries more leverage than it did at the end of June: net debt stood at 3.13 times adjusted EBITDA at the end of September, up from 2.68 times at the end of June, and management tied the rise to its purchase of spectrum licenses from EchoStar at the end of July.

Management plans to pay down debt using excess cash, along with 2027 proceeds from closing its fiber joint venture and selling its AT&T Mexico wireless business. Net debt against adjusted EBITDA is the number to watch in the January 2027 report.

Retiring AT&T's Copper Network

AT&T is moving customers off its old copper lines. In July 2026, management said it had approval to stop legacy services in over 30% of its wire centers, effective by late 2026. During the October 21 call, the company said that more than 100 wire centers no longer serve any legacy customers.

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (NYSEARCA:SCHD) grounds many retirement income portfolios for good reason. SCHD tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index, screens for yield and quality, and holds about $112.3 billion in net assets. Its trailing yield works out to about 2.96%. Over the past year, though, SCHD raised its payout only 1.95%. A four-stock basket of AT&T (NYSE:T), Chevron (NYSE:CVX), Merck (NYSE:MRK) and Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) pays a similar yield, and its dividends are growing faster.

Sundry Photography / iStock Editorial via Getty Images
Why Retirees Trust SCHD

SCHD spreads its money across healthcare, energy, staples, financials and industrials, so no single dividend cut can damage a retiree's income much. It has also delivered gains. The price rose 35.52% over the past year. The weak spot is the payout itself.

SCHD paid $1.0541 per share over the trailing 12 months, versus $1.0339 in the prior 12 months. The June 2026 distribution of $0.2525 came in below the $0.2602 paid a year earlier. That pace leaves little room when costs climb every year in retirement.

SCHD's holdings also overlap with the basket. As of August 31, 2026, SCHD already held Merck at 4.76% and Chevron at 4.01% of assets. AT&T and Walmart did not appear in its holdings, so the basket adds two businesses the fund doesn't own.
